t: During a covered furlough, a covered Federal law enforcement officer shall have the same rights to carry a firearm issued by the Federal Government as if the covered furlough was not in effect, including, if authorized on the day before the date on which the covered furlough begins, the right to carry a concealed firearm, if the sole reason the covered Federal law enforcement officer was placed on leave was due to the covered furlough.

fable.w: The section only preserves the firearm-carry rights of federal law enforcement officers during a furlough. The word "rights" might suggest a legal entitlement or right to sue, but it refers to federal employees' carry privileges, not to any outside party's consultation, comment, hearing, or right to challenge a federal decision. Every actor here is inside the federal government and no decision-making process is involved.
fable.s: a covered Federal law enforcement officer shall have the same rights to carry a firearm issued by the Federal Government as if the covered furlough was not in effect

opus.w: This section lets federal law enforcement officers keep their right to carry government-issued firearms during a covered furlough. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, placed on an advisory body, or given a right to sue. The word "rights" might suggest participation, but the rights belong to federal employees and have nothing to do with a federal decision process.
opus.b: This section is not participation. Someone might read "rights" and think it gives an outside party something to act on. That reading fails because the rights belong to federal law enforcement officers, who are inside the federal government. The section also involves no federal decision that outsiders take part in.
